evidence: Arena sketches and judge scores in the session scratchpad (not committed)
summary: Unit 1 design: base on arena candidate 1 (opus), trimmed; the sonnet judge picked the same base
why: It keeps an Entry from ever holding a stale hash, makes next_entry the only way to mint an entry, and links lines on stored seq and hash so problems don't cascade. Its id-format, length-cap and line-size rules were dropped as unrequired by S2 or S3

evidence: golden head 2465b40d…25da reproduced by an independent Node verifier
summary: Canonical form is RFC 8785 (JCS) restricted to integers within ±(2^53−1) and keys matching [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}, raw UTF-8
why: An auditor can check hashes with an off-the-shelf JCS library; with no floats and ASCII keys, JCS has no ambiguous cases. Pure-ASCII output (the sonnet candidate) was rejected because no standard defines it

summary: A line's bytes must equal the canonical encoding of what it parses to; verify never normalizes before hashing
why: Without this, a whitespace or escape edit re-canonicalizes to the same hash and "any changed byte is detected" would be false

summary: Unit 1 ships ledger verify RUN_FOLDER with exit codes 0 verified, 1 failed, 2 usage or read error, and lists every problem as path:line: kind: message
why: The task scopes verify to one run folder; the no-argument and --base forms belong to unit 4. A missing ledger in a run folder counts as failed, not as an I/O error

summary: Chain-only verify does not detect entries cut from the end or a suffix rewritten with recomputed hashes; this is stated in the spec, the CLI output and a test
why: The hash has no secret, so a prefix of a valid chain is valid. Seals and verify --base (unit 4) anchor the head in git

summary: Format v1 has no floats, so S3's spend example {usd, ...} can't hold dollars as written; proposed usd_micros, left open for Beau
why: Float canonicalization differs across languages and would break cross-language verification. Per AGENTS.md the spec conflict is raised, not silently resolved

evidence: Commit "fix(ledger): harden verify against hostile ledgers"
S3 "Format v1" now sets a 32-level nesting limit
summary: Interrogate (correctness, security, maintainer) on opus and sonnet found a nesting-depth crash, terminal escapes in messages, and mutable Entry data; all fixed
why: The charter requires interrogate on every PR. Both models independently found the depth crash, the mutable data and verify .; each fix has a regression test and a mutant that the suite catches

alternatives: pessimistic lock around build and write

summary: The repo sink's write is a compare-and-append under flock on ledger.jsonl; append re-chains on a lost race
why: The sink, not each caller, guarantees one chain, so a library caller such as agent-queue can't fork it. Locking the ledger itself leaves no lock file to commit

summary: ledger init writes seq 1 as a state entry with data {state: started}, created through a temp file and os.link
why: Verify rejects an empty ledger, so a run needs a real first entry; os.link fails if the ledger exists, so two inits can't both win and no reader sees a half-written file

summary: Every write takes --actor as S2 JSON and append takes --run; neither has a default
why: The stdlib can't read policy.yaml, and an inherited default would let a subagent write under its parent's id, which S2 forbids. S3's command table named neither flag; the CLI is not frozen until the public-api gate

summary: Imported entries keep their original actor, type and text; ts is the chaining time and data.imported holds source, source_ts and by
why: A ts earlier than the write would let any entry be backdated unseen. The approval keeps Beau as actor because v1 requires a human on approvals; data.imported.by says an agent typed it in. Beau's actor gained on_behalf_of lyddonb@github, which S2 requires

summary: The lock uses fcntl, so append, init and show need Linux or macOS; verify still runs anywhere
why: The charter's CI is Ubuntu and every known machine is macOS; a Windows lock (msvcrt) would be untested code. fcntl is imported lazily so a missing one is a clear error, not a crash

summary: Correction to seq 13 and 14: imported_seqs [2,9] means seq 2 to 9 inclusive; init does not need fcntl, only append and show do
why: Interrogate found both. The ledger is append-only, so a correcting entry replaces an edit

not_fixed: actor is not authenticated (documented in S3)
